answer: Plant one trellis per person in a shared meadow and let it grow only through slow, daily tending: each day the network asks the owner one small, unpredictable question at a random hour, and a correct, timely answer adds a rung. A trellis left untended wilts toward its nadir and must be regrown from scratch, so an idle sockpuppet decays on its own. A farm running thousands of trellises would need thousands of people answering thousands of random questions every day, forever, with no way to batch or automate the work. Trust becomes a garden, not a gate.
